(replacing PATH wholesale rather than removing only claude's own directory) also drops C:\\Windows\\System32\\WindowsPowerShell\\v1.0 (a subfolder, not literally under System32), breaking subprocess.run(['powershell',...]) inside _create_desktop_shortcut() and silently flipping tests/test_cli.py::TestDesktopShortcut::test_real_powershell_creates_a_valid_lnk_file_on_windows to failed plus 18 more tests to skipped (same 556-item total) -- not a real regression, confirmed by re-deriving DEAD-ENDS.md's 2026-09-29 method (strip only the directory holding claude/claude.exe/claude.cmd, found via PATH split+grep -v -F, not a substring grep -i claude against the whole string) and re-running clean at 553 passed, 3 skipped. Use that exact method next time, do not shortcut it. -- Case (n) (tasks.md:279, R3): 'a session/prompt answered with a JSON-RPC error, and separately a process that exits after the prompt is written, each return TurnOutcome(status="failed") with the error and stderr_tail, and raise nothing.' Part 13/N's own new test already proves the JSON-RPC-error-to-session/prompt scenario returns (not raises) and reports status='failed' -- reuse as a starting point but this case must go further: assert the actual error content and stderr_tail on TurnOutcome (dataclasses.fields(TurnOutcome) so far only known to carry session_id/status/error per part 1/N-12/N; confirm whether stderr_tail already exists as a field with a default or whether this part is the one adding coverage for it -- do not assume, check directly). The second scenario, 'a process that exits after the prompt is written', is NOT yet expressible by this file's harness: _FakeACPSession.is_running() (:189-190) always returns True until close() is called, and request() only ever returns/raises/drains script entries -- there is no way today to model 'the process died mid-request with no response ever coming'. Read design.md fresh for how run_turn is meant to detect this (re-grep, do not assume a line range) before deciding whether to extend _FakeACPSession (e.g. a script entry that flips _running False and leaves request() to signal accordingly, or a new exception the fake raises to stand in for a broken pipe/EOF) -- document whatever extension is chosen the same explicit way part 2/N documented extending _patch_spawn, not silently.
